problems.title: Rational-point-count condition does not imply finite-field closed embedding
problems.original_claim: Definition2.5 no finite-field obstruction compares numbers of k'-points for every finite extension. Lemma2.6 claims this plus embedding in a smooth curve is sufficient to embed finite Y in nonempty open V of A1.
problems.location: Definition2.5 and Lemma2.6 p8; first proof sentence p9; main invocation p18
assumptions: Y is closed in smooth connected C=A1_F2 via t²+t+1
for every finite extension F_{2^m}, count Y=2 if even/0 odd; countV=2^m−2 if even/2^m odd; all inequalities hold
problems.check: A closed embedding would be a surjective map F2[t,1/P] to F4. If t maps toF2, image isF2; otherwise it is a root ofP and violates inversion. Exhausts all possibilities, proving no embedding.
problems.result: Printed sufficiency direction false under standard rational-point meaning; all hypotheses checked for every finite extension.
counterevidence: If authors intended closed points with exact residue field, definition must be clarified/strengthened; no OCR ambiguity in actual page image.
p11 special application has only two rational supports and satisfies stronger criterion.
p16 Y_N disjoint Y_(N+1) construction satisfies exact-degree availability for largeN because closed-point counts grow and needed multiplicities remain bounded.

checks.derivation: For k=F2, P=t^2+t+1, Y=Spec F4 and V=D(P), Y is finite connected and is a closed subscheme of smooth A1. For every m, Y(F_(2^m)) has 2 points if m is even and 0 otherwise; V has 2^m-2 or 2^m respectively. All printed inequalities hold. A surjection F2[t,1/P]->F4 is impossible: t in F2 cannot generate F4; t outside F2 makes the inverted P vanish.
checks.assessment: A genuine admissible counterexample to the stated sufficiency criterion, not to the principal torsor theorem.

checks.claim: Corrected criterion and intended alternative interpretation
checks.derivation: Rational counts sum d*c_d over divisors and therefore cannot control each exact-degree count separately. Exact c_d(Y)<=c_d(V), with the smooth-curve assumption, allows distinct target points for local k_d[u]/u^e components. Truncated coordinate isomorphisms with nonzero linear term extend, preserving prescribed embeddings. If k'-points was intended to mean closed points with that exact residue field, the definition must explicitly say so.
checks.assessment: Finite-field local repair verified; infinite inseparable case not newly proved.

checks.derivation: The p11 application needs only two rational supports, available even over F2. On p16 the degrees d_i N and d_i(N+1) tend to infinity with a bounded number of components; m I_q(m)>=q^m-sum_{j<=m/2}q^j supplies enough exact-degree points, uniformly over finitely many residue fields. Page18 nevertheless invokes the false general criterion after an external finite-etale cover.
checks.assessment: Major core proof-justification issue, with neither failure of that particular cover nor falsity of Theorem4.3 established. The external cover's stronger property remains expressly unverified.
